samples.summary: `slides export` still aborts the whole export when an image fetch is refused, while the docs exporters were made tolerant
samples.evidence: `packages/cli/src/commands/slides.ts:209` builds the newly-guarded `createImageFetcher` and hands it to `exportPptxCli` → `exportPptx`, whose image loop is `const { bytes, mime } = await opts.fetchImage(src);` at `packages/slides/src/export/pptx/index.ts:162` with no try/catch. The same change made `collectAndEmbedImages` (packages/docs/src/export/pdf-image-painter.ts:99) and `DocxExporter.collectImages` (packages/docs/src/export/docx-exporter.ts:448) drop-and-warn, so `docs export` survives a refused/timed-out/oversized image but `slides export` now fails outright — a new failure mode for any deck whose images live on a non-public host (self-hosted MinIO, second internal origin) that the operator has not listed in WAFFLEBASE_IMAGE_HOSTS. `packages/cli/test/slides-export.test.ts` has no image case, so nothing catches this. Fix belongs either in the pptx orchestrator or in the CLI's `exportPptxCli` wrapper (packages/cli/src/slides/pptx-export.ts:14).

samples.summary: Browser docs export now silently produces a document with images missing; the UI relied on the exporter throwing
samples.evidence: `DocxExporter.export` (docx-actions.ts:50) and `PdfExporter.export` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/pdf-actions.ts:30) are out-of-diff consumers of the exporters whose per-image failure now becomes a `console.warn` (packages/docs/src/export/docx-exporter.ts:452, packages/docs/src/export/pdf-image-painter.ts:63) instead of a rejection. `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-export-button.tsx:89/97` wraps the call in a runExport that only surfaces a thrown error, so in the browser — where there is no SSRF guard making a refusal ordinary — a failed image download now yields a silently incomplete download with no user-visible signal. `collectAndEmbedImages`/`ImageErrorReporter` are not re-exported from `packages/docs/src/index.ts`, so the frontend cannot even wire the new `onImageError` reporter. docs/design/cli.md:1204-1211 acknowledges this as follow-up work.

samples.summary: The new catch also swallows decode/embed failures, contradicting this function's own documented contract
samples.evidence: The try block added at pdf-image-painter.ts:81-101 spans `blob.arrayBuffer()`, `embedPng/embedJpg` and the browser-only `embedAsPng`, so the documented behaviour on line 41 — “That conversion path is browser-only — Node/jsdom callers that hit a non-PNG/JPEG src will get a clear error.” — no longer holds: a WebP/GIF image exported to PDF from the CLI or from jsdom is now dropped with a console.warn. The docstring at line 41 was left describing the old contract.

samples.summary: New non-JSON `console.warn` lines land on the CLI's stderr, which agents parse, and `--quiet` cannot suppress them
samples.evidence: `warnImageError` (pdf-image-painter.ts:63) and the DOCX equivalent (packages/docs/src/export/docx-exporter.ts:452) write plain prose to stderr from inside the export libraries. `packages/cli/README.md:139` documents stderr as carrying `a single JSON line`, and the CLI's own suppressible progress notices go through `opts.quiet`, which these warnings bypass entirely (they are emitted inside @wafflebase/docs, which knows nothing about `--quiet`). An agent that JSON-parses stderr after `wafflebase docs export` now sees an unparseable line.

samples.summary: `fileUrl()` can now throw synchronously during React render because `seg()` refuses `.`/`..`
samples.evidence: `fileUrl` (packages/frontend/src/api/files.ts:23) now calls `seg(documentId)`, which throws for `.`/`..`. It is invoked in render/props positions at packages/frontend/src/app/shared/shared-document.tsx:726 and packages/frontend/src/app/files/pdf-collab.tsx:139, where the id comes from `useParams`/a resolved share link. A crafted `/f/%2E%2E` style route param would turn a 404 into an uncaught render exception (blank screen) rather than a failed request. The async API callers are unaffected because the throw becomes a rejected promise there.

finding.summary: `slides export` still aborts the whole export when an image fetch is refused, while the docs exporters were made tolerant
finding.evidence: `packages/cli/src/commands/slides.ts:209` builds the newly-guarded `createImageFetcher` and hands it to `exportPptxCli` → `exportPptx`, whose image loop is `const { bytes, mime } = await opts.fetchImage(src);` at `packages/slides/src/export/pptx/index.ts:162` with no try/catch. The same change made `collectAndEmbedImages` (packages/docs/src/export/pdf-image-painter.ts:99) and `DocxExporter.collectImages` (packages/docs/src/export/docx-exporter.ts:448) drop-and-warn, so `docs export` survives a refused/timed-out/oversized image but `slides export` now fails outright — a new failure mode for any deck whose images live on a non-public host (self-hosted MinIO, second internal origin) that the operator has not listed in WAFFLEBASE_IMAGE_HOSTS. `packages/cli/test/slides-export.test.ts` has no image case, so nothing catches this. Fix belongs either in the pptx orchestrator or in the CLI's `exportPptxCli` wrapper (packages/cli/src/slides/pptx-export.ts:14).

verdict.reason: Every claimed location checks out. `packages/cli/src/commands/slides.ts:209` builds the newly-guarded fetcher and passes it to `exportPptxCli`; the wrapper at `packages/cli/src/slides/pptx-export.ts:12-18` awaits `opts.imageFetcher!(src)` at :14 with no error handling; and `packages/slides/src/export/pptx/index.ts:162` awaits `opts.fetchImage(src)` inside a bare loop, so any rejection aborts the entire export. Meanwhile the same shared fetcher's new throw conditions (non-allowlisted private host per image-fetcher.ts:53/:104-120, 30s timeout :67, 25MB cap :73) were absorbed on the docs side: `packages/docs/src/export/pdf-image-painter.ts:99-101` catches and calls `onImageError`, and `packages/docs/src/export/docx-exporter.ts:448-455` catches, warns "Skipping image", and continues, with a comment stating that a refused image "must not cost the whole export". The slides consumer of the changed contract was not updated, leaving `slides export` failing outright where `docs export` degrades — a cross-file inconsistency invisible from the diff, squarely in the blast-radius lane (behaviour change to an exported symbol with an unconsidered consumer). No guard makes the path unreachable: the command only short-circuits on --dry-run (slides.ts:199-206), and exportPptx requires fetchImage whenever images exist (pptx/index.ts:154-160). No named refutation ground applies.

finding.summary: Browser docs export now silently produces a document with images missing; the UI relied on the exporter throwing
finding.evidence: `DocxExporter.export` (docx-actions.ts:50) and `PdfExporter.export` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/pdf-actions.ts:30) are out-of-diff consumers of the exporters whose per-image failure now becomes a `console.warn` (packages/docs/src/export/docx-exporter.ts:452, packages/docs/src/export/pdf-image-painter.ts:63) instead of a rejection. `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-export-button.tsx:89/97` wraps the call in a runExport that only surfaces a thrown error, so in the browser — where there is no SSRF guard making a refusal ordinary — a failed image download now yields a silently incomplete download with no user-visible signal. `collectAndEmbedImages`/`ImageErrorReporter` are not re-exported from `packages/docs/src/index.ts`, so the frontend cannot even wire the new `onImageError` reporter. docs/design/cli.md:1204-1211 acknowledges this as follow-up work.

verdict.reason: All claimed locations verified. docx-exporter.ts:448-455 catches a failed image fetch and only console.warns (pushing an empty rId entry that buildPartRelsXml at :393-395 filters out); pdf-image-painter.ts:80-102 catches fetch/decode/embed failures and routes them to onImageError, whose default warnImageError (:17-20) only console.warns. The out-of-diff browser consumers exist and inherit this: docx-actions.ts:50 and pdf-actions.ts:30-36 both pass docsImageFetcher, which throws on !res.ok (export-utils.ts:52-54) — precisely the failure now swallowed. docs-export-button.tsx:41-62 reports success unconditionally and only shows an error toast from a thrown exception, and both menu items (:89, :97) use it; the component is mounted at docs-detail.tsx:202, so the path is reachable in the shipped app. The frontend cannot even opt out: packages/docs/src/index.ts:179-196 does not export collectAndEmbedImages or ImageErrorReporter, PdfExportOptions (pdf-exporter.ts:31-39) has no onImageError field, and pdf-exporter.ts:132-134 calls collectAndEmbedImages with no reporter; DocxExporter has no reporter seam at all. This is in-lane for blast-radius: a behaviour change to exported symbols whose consumers in another package still rely on the old throwing contract, leaving them silently producing incomplete documents. docs/design/cli.md:1204-1211 and docs/tasks/active/20260811-cli-upstream-error-envelope-lessons.md:158-162 explicitly acknowledge the browser exporters inherit the swallow with no user-visible signal — documentation of a limitation is not a guard and does not refute the defect. No refutation ground (not-present, already-guarded, out-of-scope, counterexample) applies.

finding.summary: Reviewer did not produce a valid verdict: review: every credential in the pool (3) was retired — nothing left to fail over to

verdict.reason: The finding's text is not a claim about repository code — it is verbatim the review harness's own synthetic placeholder. scripts/agent/review-panel.mjs:1656 emits `Reviewer did not produce a valid verdict: ${err.message}` whenever a lens throws, and the interpolated message is produced by poolExhaustedError() at scripts/agent/ask.mjs:630-637 (`every credential in the pool (N) was retired — nothing left to fail over to`, kind "pool-exhausted"; pinned by ask.test.mjs:302,321,341). So the report says the blast-radius lens run itself aborted on credential exhaustion. It names no file, line, changed symbol, caller, or bypassing site, and matches no item in the blast-radius lane (no bypassed guard, no changed contract with stale callers, no removed export, no violated invariant); there is no location that could be edited to fix it. The repository routes this exact string on a separate infrastructure path rather than as a review finding: rounds.mjs:561-565 excludes it from finding-based stall analysis, and review-round-guard.mjs:188 with guard-verdict.mjs:22 pages a human under "invalid-verdict", with infra-summary.test.mjs:36 pinning the classification — so dropping it from the findings merge gate does not suppress the outage signal. I also considered the alternative reading that the exhaustion evidences an over-eager retirement bug in the changed failover code (ask.mjs:600-637, token-pool.mjs), but the finding asserts no such site or contract, and a quota/credential outage is the documented ordinary cause of this error.
